learning: Hypotheses: (1) bend line loss is a bend-entry speed limit, so a further speed reduction should lower s-bend and slalom line_loss_events toward 2.0; (2) the s-bend jitter (0.37) is under-damped, so kd 0.6 should bring steering_oscillation down; (3) if line loss stays at 2.0 or more on the s-bend, the geometry is the next lever (wheel_track 0.14 m, as the Builder proposed). Watch completion_time on the oval, because the speed margin is the limit on how far base_speed can drop.
notes: Holds the iteration-9 geometry and tests a controller-only step: base_speed 1.2 to 1.0 for slower bend entry, and kd 0.5 to 0.6 to damp the bend jitter (steering_oscillation 0.37 on the s-bend). The expected oval finish time is about 2.3 s, still under 3 s.
rationale: Iteration 9 is the best design so far (412.7). Its geometry is the iteration-8 layout, which is also the one the Builder holds for iteration 10: five sensors at x = -0.025 to +0.025 m, y = 0.075 m, 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.18 by 0.12 m, mass 0.5 kg. The iteration-9 controller change (base_speed 1.4 to 1.2, kd 0.4 to 0.5) is what produced the gain. Oval finished 20 of 20 at 1.91 s mean, so there is still roughly 1 s of margin under the 3 s limit. The slalom line loss fell from 3.0 to 2.1, which supports the view that a slower bend entry helps. The s-bend improved in score (89 to 237), but its line loss rose to 2.3 and steering_oscillation rose to 0.37 on the bends, so the bends now show jitter, not just under-response. Two moves follow from this. First, lower base_speed a further step to 1.0, which gives the 0.04 m lookahead more time on bend entry. The oval should finish in roughly 2.3 s by scaling the 1.91 s mean, which keeps it inside 3 s. Second, raise kd from 0.5 to 0.6 to damp the bend oscillation, where kd has previously reduced jitter (0.20 to 0.16 when kd went 0.3 to 0.4). kp stays at 4.0 and ki at 0.1, so the change is limited to speed and damping. I expect the s-bend line loss to fall toward 2.0 and the slalom toward 2.0, with the oval finish rate held at 1.0. This is a prediction, not a measured result. The Builder's geometry is unchanged, so the controller result can be read cleanly.
